_purpose: The declared set of repository guards. Before this file existed, the set was
implicit in the YAML text of .github/workflows/ and in GitHub's branch
protection settings, and the two were never confronted: removing a guard's
`run:` line from ci.yml turned nothing red (issue #1702), and a guard that
runs in a workflow nobody requires is decorative at merge time (#1698).
workflows AND with the filesystem. The filesystem half is what makes the
registry impossible to shrink silently: every guard-shaped script under
scripts/ must appear here, either under `guards` or under `unwired` with a
written reason. Deleting an entry does not remove the obligation — the script
is still on disk, so the suite demands an accounting for it.

_schema.script: repo-relative path, the identity of the guard
_schema.workflow: the workflow file whose job invokes it
_schema.job: the job key inside that workflow
_schema.required: true when a failure of `job` must fail the single required check (CI Success)
_schema.mode: strict = a finding fails the build; warn = it does not (see exit_condition)
_schema.exit_condition: mandatory when mode is warn: what has to happen for it to become strict
_schema.self_test: unittest module that proves the guard refuses; null when none exists
_schema.self_test_required: true when that module runs inside a required job
_schema.blind_spot: known limit of the guard's reach, with the issue tracking it
_schema.required_via: when the guard lives outside ci.yml: the ci.yml job that calls its workflow, and through which it becomes required

_json_not_yaml: gate-contracts.yml runs these suites with a bare actions/setup-python and
installs nothing, so importing PyYAML here would be an ImportError in CI — a
guard that cannot run. json is stdlib everywhere. Same reasoning that keeps
the workflow parsers in test_ci_gate_reachability.py regex-based.
